cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to believers living as exiles, scattered across a bunch of regions (1 Peter 1:1). He just told them to repay insults with blessing, not with more insults (1 Peter 3:9). Now he asks them a question: "Who can harm you if you are zealous for what is good?"
What a question. But Peter keeps it REAL: even when you're all in for what's good, you could still suffer for doing what's right.

cards.question: Peter says that even if the believers suffer for doing what's right, they are blessed.

cards.text: Then Peter quotes the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 8:12): "Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken." Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS, and every time somebody yanked it open looking for tape, I got SHAKEN.

cards.question: Instead of fearing, Peter tells the believers to sanctify Christ as Lord. Where?

cards.text: Next, Peter says to always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks. Always, friend. Not sometimes. Not when you feel like it. Not after your second cup of coffee. ALWAYS.

cards.question: When someone asks, what does Peter say the believers should be ready to explain?

answers.text: The reason for the hope in them

cards.question: Peter says to answer anyone who asks with gentleness and respect.

cards.text: Gentle and respectful, friend, not like that one person in the group chat who answers EVERYTHING in all caps. And Peter says to keep a clear conscience while they do it.

cards.question: Some people slander the believers. What does Peter say the believers' good behavior in Christ may do to those people?

cards.text: Then Peter says suffering may come, if it's God's will. But not all suffering is the same.

cards.question: If suffering comes and it's God's will, Peter says suffering for doing evil is better than suffering for doing good.

cards.text: Now Peter points the believers to Christ. Because Christ ALSO suffered for sins.

cards.question: Peter says Christ suffered for sins. How many times?
Peter says Christ suffered for sins to bring the believers to God.

cards.text: Christ suffered as the righteous for the unrighteous. Then Peter says it plainly: He was put to death in the body.

cards.question: After Christ was put to death in the body, Peter says He stayed dead.

cards.text: Death did NOT get the last word. Peter says He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit.
Stay with me, friend, because this part goes DEEP. Peter goes on, "in whom He also went and preached to the spirits in prison", spirits who disobeyed long ago.

cards.question: The spirits in prison disobeyed long ago, while God waited patiently. In whose days?

cards.text: Noah's the man God told to build an ark (Genesis 6:14), and God waited patiently while it was being built. Patiently, friend. Meanwhile I'm over here pressing the elevator button nine times like it's going to hurry up.

cards.question: In the ark, only eight souls were saved through ___.

cards.text: Then Peter takes that water from Noah's day and ties it to something in the believers' own day.

cards.question: Peter says the water of Noah's day symbolizes the ___ that now saves the believers too.
Peter says baptism is about washing dirt off the body.
If baptism isn't about dirt, what does Peter call it?

answers.text: A pledge of a clear conscience toward God
A promise to keep every law of God
A record of good works before God

cards.text: And baptism saves through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God. Let that sink in, baker: that's where He IS.

cards.question: Jesus is at the right hand of God. What does Peter say about the angels, authorities and powers?
